alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ fronted by the ASV as the verse-opening For; rule 15 permits the reordering.

Relative pronoun alone. No ἄν or ἐάν stands here, so the -soever of whosoever is the pronoun's own generalizing force and rules 50 and 72 are not in question; no substantival article stands here either, so rule 80 does not arise.
Rule 9: the modal auxiliary shall rides with the subjunctive and the head is the lexical verb keep.
Rule 19: the article surfaces as the. The attributive ὅλον does not displace it, being a quantifying adjective inside the phrase rather than a determiner (rules 38 and 49 speak of demonstratives).
Attributive adjective standing bare, the article having taken the determiner under rule 58's closing clause (τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν → the only true God).
Head noun, bare after the article took the.

The ASV writes the adversative connective as and yet; both words answer to δέ, which is expressed, so rule 98's added juncture is not in question. Head on yet, the word carrying the adversative sense δέ contributes here; the competing reading heads on and as the more ordinary corpus gloss of δέ, and rule 91's operational test would support it, but rule 17 refuses a word chosen merely because it stands first and the concessive force is what this clause needs.
Second subjunctive under the same shall; the auxiliary is not repeated in the English, so the verb stands alone.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes ἐν.

Substantival numeral adjective expanded with the supplied generic noun point (ASV italics, rule 11 making that evidence only). Rule 17's generic-noun clause holds the head on the numeral, as it does for all things and good thing.
Rules 7 and 9: the supplied subject he and the perfect auxiliary is ride with the verb, headed on the lexical become.
Predicate adjective; the copula is already spent on the expressed γέγονεν, so rules 53 and 63 do not arise.
Genitive governed by ἔνοχος; rule 17 keeps the head on the noun-equivalent all with the case preposition of riding along. No article stands here, so rule 21 is not in question.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged: every unit's edges and head survive the audit. All 13 source and all 19 target ids are partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented, added or noncompositional unit is needed anywhere in this verse.

Only one unit is materially contested, δέ → and yet. I kept the head on yet and expanded the note to name rule 91's operational test as the strongest argument for the competing head on and, since and is the more ordinary corpus rendering of δέ while yet carries the adversative force this clause turns on. A later reader flipping this head should flip only the head, not the edges: both words answer to the expressed δέ, so neither is added under rule 98.

Audited the article sequence ὅλον τὸν νόμον under rule 13. τὸν takes the English the under rule 19 and is not emptied: rules 38 and 49 empty an article only where a demonstrative occupies the determiner slot, and ὅλον is a quantifying adjective, not a demonstrative. Rule 58 does not reach it either, that rule being scoped to an anarthrous adjective-plus-noun phrase; its closing clause is what puts the determiner on the article and leaves whole bare.

Checked ὅστις against rules 50, 72 and 80. No ἄν or ἐάν stands in the verse, so the -soever is not a particle's, and no substantival article stands with it, so rule 80's πᾶς ὁ pattern is not this construction. The pronoun takes whosoever alone.

Checked ἑνί → one point and ἔνοχος πάντων → guilty of all for the generic-noun head trap. Rule 17 holds the head on the numeral one rather than the italicized supplied point, and on all rather than the case preposition of; ἔνοχος keeps a bare guilty because γέγονεν is expressed and no copula is supplied for rule 53 to place.

Variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.10.v007 is underdetermined with the base fallback still among the compatible readings r00-base, r01 and r02, so it carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE mark and rule 97 is not in play. Both s006 and s007 align normally and no textual decision was taken inside this file, per rule 12.
